All package structure is derived directly from the source text (torah_150.txt), which is the shortest recorded teaching in this dataset — 2 lines. The lemma is the talmudic aggadah (Sotah 36b; Tanchuma Vayeshev) about Yosef seeing the image of his father's form (דְּמוּת דְּיוֹקְנוֹ שֶׁל אָבִיו) at the moment of his temptation by Potiphar's wife. The Rebbe's teaching is a brief reflection on the hidden/concealed nature of the miracle: how the image appeared is a very hidden matter; the person involved (Yosef, and certainly Yaakov) does not know the mechanism; and this hiddenness IS the quality/greatness (מַעֲלַת) of the trial (נִסָּיוֹן). There is no explicit בְּחִינַת / הוא בחינת / נקרא language in the text. The implicit bechina-type identification is: מַעֲלַת הַנִּסָּיוֹן (the excellence of the trial) IS דְּבָרִים נִסְתָּרִים וּמְכֻסִּים (hidden and concealed matters) — the hiddenness constitutes and defines the greatness. The entire teaching is within the good domain (the protective power of ancestral/paternal merit; the wonder of divine hiddenness that enables spiritual protection). No evil mirror is developed or implied in the text.

packages.label: דְּמוּת דְּיוֹקֶן וְנִסָּיוֹן הַנִּסְתָּר
packages.label_en: The Hidden Image and the Concealed Trial
packages.reason: This teaching contains a single thematic cluster, centered on three mutually illuminating concepts: (1) דְּמוּת דְּיוֹקְנוֹ שֶׁל אָבִיו — the image of his father's form, which appeared to Yosef to protect him from sin; (2) נִסָּיוֹן — the trial/test, specifically the trial of sexual temptation that Yosef faced; (3) נִסְתָּר / דְּבָרִים נִסְתָּרִים וּמְכֻסִּים — the hidden and concealed nature of how the image appeared. All three share the same essential nature within this teaching: they all belong to the domain of the miraculous hidden dimension of spiritual protection. The implicit bechina declared by the Rebbe is: מַעֲלַת הַנִּסָּיוֹן (the excellence/quality of the trial) IS constituted by the hiddenness — the very fact that these are דְּבָרִים נִסְתָּרִים וּמְכֻסִּים mִבְּנֵי אָדָם IS the greatness of what occurred. The image (דְּמוּת דְּיוֹקֶן) IS a hidden matter (דָּבָר נִסְתָּר) by its very nature — not explainable, not knowable even to Yaakov himself. The Rebbe does not explain the mechanism; he declares it to be opaque and presents that opacity as the defining feature. These three dimensions — the image, the trial, and the hiddenness — all refer to the same essential phenomenon from different angles. They cannot be separated into distinct packages because the teaching is too brief and does not develop independent conceptual clusters. This is a good package because the entire discourse is about a positive spiritual protection: the father's image appearing to save his son from sin. The polarity is unambiguously good: Yosef withstands temptation, the miracle is of the side of holiness, the father-image is the tzaddik/patriarch protecting his descendants.
merge_notes: The three nodes form one inseparable cluster — the teaching is too short and thematically unified to split into sub-packages. The implicit bechina structure is: דמות דיוקן ↔ דבר נסתר (the image IS a hidden matter), and מעלת הנסיון ↔ דברים נסתרים ומכוסים (the greatness of the trial IS constituted by the hiddenness). Since the single teaching makes all three concepts facets of one reality — the miraculous hidden protection that enabled Yosef's trial — they belong together in one package.
